chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Fazalah, from Dawud ibn Farqad, who said:
We were in the presence of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) in Makkah, and Dawud ibn Ali was with us. So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to me: 'Dawud ibn Ali said to me,
What do you say, O Abu Abdillah, regarding the dove we hunted and clipped (its wings)?
I said: 'It is plucked and fed. When it is straight (wings grown back), it is freed.'

key_terms.اسْتَوَتْ: It became straight/even (referring to wing growth)
key_terms.قَمَارِيَّ: A type of dove or pigeon

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a hunted dove with clipped wings according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi highlights the practical application of expiation (kaffarah) for hunting in the sacred precincts, specifically addressing the temporary captivity of a dove with clipped wings. Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) prescribes a restorative process—plucking, feeding, and waiting for the wings to straighten—before release, reflecting the Shia juristic emphasis on restoring the animal's natural state as part of the penance. This incident, occurring in Mecca, underscores the specific legal nuances applied to game hunted within the Haram boundaries.
